transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Rivera (CTO, Amaris Health), Jordan Lee (Product PM), Elliot Chen (Infra Lead)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) deployments for a rollout Q1 2027. Key asks: per-route cost allocation, token-level breakdowns, audit logs and encryption, benchmark plan for latency under 50ms p50, and an estimate for committed capacity pricing.

Topics:
- Console: usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns and chargeback
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Observability: traces, token-level cost, error budgets
- Security/compliance: SOC 2, KMS integration, audit logs, SSO
- Next steps and benchmark plan

Transcript: 
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, Priya and I will run through the console, the usage analytics screen and then the per route dashboards, um and then go into a bit about dedicated and private options, quick q's at any time.
[00:18] Maya Rivera: Thanks Alex, appreciate it. Our infra lead Elliot and Jordan in product are on, we're mainly focused on cost and compliance, we've got a pilot early Q1 so timeline is tight.
[00:29] Priya Shah: Great, we'll try to keep it tight. Starting on the console home, you can see token consumption over time, split by model and route, so if you have a support bot route and a search route you can attribute costs per route.
[00:44] Jordan Lee: Quick q, how granular is the per-route? Can we do per-endpoint and per-team?
[00:51] Priya Shah: Yes per-endpoint, per-route, we also tag by team or product. The cost breakdown is token-level, we show prompt vs completion tokens and an estimated cost column. There's also export to csv and api access for chargeback.
[01:12] Elliot Chen: Is that token cost based on hosted pricing or does it take into account dedicated reserved capacity?
[01:18] Priya Shah: Good callout, we show both. For hosted API we show current unit costs; for Dedicated we show an amortized cost per token based on committed GPU capacity and your commit size, and for Private we show a projected cost model factoring infra you're running plus inference efficiency, quantization, etc. Sometimes the label on the console says "amortized commit" and the transcript might read "amortized commit" but that shows the blended unit economics.
[01:44] Maya Rivera: We have a weird mix of bursty traffic and steady nightly batch jobs, so curious about autoscaling and predictable latency.
[01:53] Alex Morgan: Right, there are a couple of levers - batching, prefix caching (we do KV cache, sometimes auto transcriptions say KV cash), and routing policies. The console has dashboards where you can filter by sequence length distribution which helps pick kernel configs and batching windows.
[02:15] Jordan Lee: Can you show an example of a route breakdown?
[02:20] Priya Shah: Sure, switching to the per-route dashboard - this is the support-bot route, you can see 95th percentile latency per model version, token usage by user segment, and the cost heatmap. We also surface regression alerts tied to prompt sets - if a new model rollout increases token usage or changes output quality, the evals hook flags it.
[02:46] Elliot Chen: For our security team, how do audit logs look? Do we get token-level logs or just call metadata?
[02:54] Priya Shah: By default we store call metadata and aggregated cost traces in the console; for Private deployments you can enable full audit logs and ship them to your SIEM. We also integrate with KMS/HSM for key management.
[03:09] Maya Rivera: SOC 2 and data residency are big for us, can you share your SOC 2 report and any info on regional hosting?
[03:17] Alex Morgan: Absolutely, we'll send the SOC 2 and the compliance packet. We have regional hosting options in NA/EU and private VPC packs for strict residency.
[03:28] Jordan Lee: On the amortized cost per token for Dedicated, what's the typical delta vs hosted?
[03:34] Priya Shah: It varies a lot on QPS and model family; rough ballpark - for steady high throughput using quantized models you can see 30-60% lower unit cost on Dedicated vs hosted, especially if you're able to use batching and cache effectively. But for low throughput or spiky workloads hosted can be cheaper due to no commit.
[03:58] Elliot Chen: Do you support mixed routing? Like send critical low-latency traffic to dedicated and overflow to hosted?
[04:05] Alex Morgan: Yes, smart routing is exactly we built - route by latency SLO, cost threshold, or region, with automated fallback to a compatible model. That way you keep critical traffic on dedicated and offload spikes to hosted.
[04:21] Maya Rivera: What's involved to test our workload? We want to run a benchmark against our request traces.
[04:27] Priya Shah: We usually ask for a representative sample of traces, schema and token distribution. We'll run a benchmark on our infra (or provide a harness you can run) and report p50/p95 latencies, throughput, and token costs. We'll include recommended quantization and batching configs.
[04:44] Jordan Lee: Any gotchas on metrics? We care about per-route chargeback for product teams.
[04:49] Priya Shah: The console supports tags and per-route attribution; one hiccup is if you have large shared context or long KV cache entries they can skew per-request cost allocation, we call that out in the docs. There's also an api for exporting detailed usage so you can feed it into your internal chargeback system.
[05:09] Elliot Chen: How precise is the token accounting when using external prompt engineering layers? We have pre- and post-processing that might be outside Redwood.
[05:17] Alex Morgan: We surface token counts based on the call payload we see. If you pre-process upstream, best practice is to pass Redwood the final prompt; otherwise you can instrument locally and join datasets. We'll show a combined view if you share traces.
[05:31] Maya Rivera: About security again, we need SSO (SAML), RBAC and per-route ACLs for teams.
[05:38] Priya Shah: All supported - SSO via SAML/OIDC, role-based access controls and per-route access rules. For Private customers we can also integrate with your AD/Okta directly.
[05:49] Jordan Lee: Any mention of competitors during call? Noted that Anthropic and OpenAI have different pricing models - might be relevant for procurement.
[05:58] Alex Morgan: Yep, good to consider. Redwood's angle is production economics and predictable cost controls, plus tooling for rollouts and observability.
[06:07] Maya Rivera: Ok, let's talk deliverables. We want a pricing estimate and a benchmark run, also security docs.
[06:13] Alex Morgan: We'll do that.
[06:15] Priya Shah: I'll own the benchmark plan. We'll need a sample of traces and your latency targets.
[06:22] Elliot Chen: Latency target: p50 < 50ms for simple prompt paths, p95 under 200ms for interactive. Token volume estimate - we're at about 120M tokens/month currently across product teams, with a peak QPS of ~35.
[06:38] Alex Morgan: Great that's helpful. We'll model three scenarios: hosted only, dedicated commit, and private deployment cost estimates.
[06:44] Jordan Lee: Also curious about cost impact of quantization on quality - we'll need to see evals for regen rates.
[06:51] Priya Shah: We tie regressions to prompt sets in the console so you can see quality changes. For regression-prone workloads we recommend canary rollouts and automatic fallback to prior model.
[07:03] Maya Rivera: Are there limits to streaming or tool calling? We do a fair amount of function/tool calls from the bot.
[07:10] Alex Morgan: Streaming and tool calling supported. Cost and latency for tool calls are shown per-route.
[07:15] Alex Morgan: Ok, wrapping up - recap of next steps and owners.
[07:20] Maya Rivera: Thanks both.
